newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador resignations said matter of courtesy.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador resignations said matter of courtesy.

text.p: Three Ecuadoran cabinet ministers resigned on Tuesday but officials said they were making a gesture of courtesy traditional at the end of the year and may stay in their jobs.

"Some ministers present their resignations as an act of courtesy towards the president -- to give him the option of renewing his cabinet or keeping it as it is," an Interior Ministry official told Reuters.
But President Abdala Bucaram said "I am analysing the resignations." His spokesman, Fernando Artieda, said, "The possibility of President Bucaram's accepting one of the resignations is not remote."
Bucaram was due to hold a news conference later on Tuesday.
Housing Minister Victor Sicouret said that he was resigning, along with Energy Minister Alfredo Adum and Industry Minister Jorge Marun.
"We are freeing up the president's hands, so he can inject fresh air into the cabinet," Sicouret told reporters.
An Energy Ministry spokesman said Adum's resignation would not be accepted.
"The most likely thing would be for the president to ratify him in his position," the spokesman said.
Adum, who oversees the oil sector that makes Ecuador's largest export earnings, faces two criminal charges for alleged assault and unjustified dismissal of workers at state firm Petroecuador.
He also faces impeachment in Congress for alleged irregularities.
